topic: AI Chatbots: OpenAI vs Google’s Slow Burn
description: A timeline comparison of how OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini fought for consumer mindshare after the 2022 launch—then flipped the market with 2023–2025 momentum, while Google’s rollout pace created dramatic share swings.
youtube_description:
⏱️ Timeline Comparison: AI Chatbots — OpenAI vs Google’s Slow Burn

In this chart-race style video, we visualize how one company sparked global demand, while the other spent more time scaling its rollout. We track the rise of branded chatbot searches (ChatGPT, Gemini) against the broader pull of the “AI chatbot” category and the slow decline of generic “chatbot” traffic.

📌 Chapters:
0:00 — The pre-2022 baseline (why “AI chatbot” was still niche)
0:35 — 2022: ChatGPT ignites the category (brand search jumps)
1:20 — 2023: OpenAI momentum becomes a daily habit (race widens)
2:05 — 2024: Gemini arrives with stronger positioning (compression phase)
2:55 — 2025: Google catches more mindshare (but not all the way)
3:40 — 2026: The market matures—brands stabilize at higher levels

✅ What to watch for:
• How quickly ChatGPT overtakes generic “chatbot” searches
• Whether Gemini’s slope steepens after earlier lag
• How the overall category stays elevated even as generic interest fades

instagram_caption:
🚀 OpenAI detonated the AI chatbot category… and Google had to sprint uphill.

Let’s rewind to when “AI chatbot” wasn’t a daily headline. In 2019–2021, chatbot interest was mostly quiet—brand-level demand barely existed (ChatGPT effectively 0–3 on our index, Gemini ~2 at its peak). The category itself hovered low: “AI chatbot” was only an 8→14 range, and generic “chatbot” traffic still owned the attention (46–49).

Then came 2022. ChatGPT launched and immediately reshaped behavior. Search interest for ChatGPT exploded from ~22 to a new reality—our index jumps to 22 in 2022, and by 2023 it rockets to 78. That’s the moment the market stops being “experiments” and becomes “utility.” Meanwhile generic “chatbot” traffic starts bleeding: it slips from 44 (2022) down to 36 (2023). People weren’t searching for “a chatbot”—they were searching for *the one they heard about*.

Google’s Gemini began with a smaller foothold: 6 in 2022, then rising to 28 by 2023. The story wasn’t “no progress”—it was *pace*. In 2024, Gemini finally steepens to 55 as distribution, product integration, and user awareness improve. And by 2025 it reaches 59, climbing again in 2026 to 63.

Here’s the chart-race truth: the AI chatbot market magnet stays strong. The broader “AI chatbot” category climbs from 32 (2022) to 71 (2024) and peaks around 76 in 2026. But generic “chatbot” traffic continues to decline—28 by 2026—because the market is now brand-driven.

So in your head, who won the chatbot era: OpenAI’s ChatGPT habit loop… or Google’s Gemini catching up? Drop your pick in the comments, and follow for more chart-race timelines.
facebook_caption:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini entered a newly formed consumer market in the early-to-mid 2020s, but they scaled at different speeds. From 2019–2021, “AI chatbot” interest remained niche (category index rising from 8 to 14), while generic chatbot traffic stayed dominant (46–49). 

In 2022, ChatGPT’s launch triggered a step-change: ChatGPT brand interest rose to 22, while generic “chatbot” traffic fell to 44. The momentum continued into 2023, when ChatGPT surged to 78 and generic interest dropped further to 36—indicating users were shifting from generic discovery to branded daily use.

Google’s Gemini showed a later acceleration: its index reached 6 in 2022 and climbed to 28 by 2023. By 2024, Gemini’s curve steepened to 55, and it continued to gain to 59 (2025) and 63 (2026). Throughout the same period, the overall “AI chatbot” category remained elevated (32 in 2022 to 76 in 2026), but the non-brand “chatbot” traffic steadily declined (28 in 2026), reinforcing that the market became brand-led rather than generic.

Hot take: ChatGPT didn’t just launch—it *trained* the internet to search for “the chatbot.”

From 2019–2021 it was basically niche (ChatGPT ~0–3, Gemini ~2; generic chatbot traffic still ~46–49). Then 2022 hits: ChatGPT brand interest jumps to 22 and by 2023 it’s 78. That same year generic “chatbot” traffic drops to 36—people stopped searching for generic.

Gemini starts later (6 in 2022 → 28 in 2023), then the slope really improves in 2024 (55), and keeps climbing to 59 in 2025 and 63 in 2026.

Meanwhile the category stays hot: “AI chatbot” rises to ~76 by 2026, but generic keeps shrinking (28).

Who’s winning in your daily usage—ChatGPT or Gemini? 👀
